title: Richmond Home Energy Rebates 2026: Heat Pumps, Insulation and Water Heaters
desc: Richmond rebates for 2026 from BC Hydro, FortisBC and CleanBC, shaped by Richmond's mix of 81,080 households and one of the mildest winters in the group.
badge: Heat pumps up to $4,000 for electric homes
lead: Richmond's 81,080 households live in one of the mildest climates in the group: the January average low is 1.5°C and the record low in our 2015 to 2024 data is only -14.4°C.
cards_heading: What you can claim in Richmond in 2026
cards_intro: Amounts come from the program pages we re-read on October 2, 2026. Each card is a maximum, and most depend on how your home is heated.

cards.title: Whole-home heat pump
cards.note: Must replace electric heat such as baseboards or an electric furnace, meet 100% of the heating load at -5C and be installed by a Home Performance Contractor Network member.

cards.title: Partial heat pump
cards.note: For a heat pump that covers at least half of the heating load while replacing electric heat.

cards.title: Limited-time bonus
cards.note: Extra money on heat pump installs completed between August 1 and October 31, 2026.

cards.title: Income-qualified switch from gas, oil or propane
cards.note: CleanBC pays by income level (Level 3 / Level 2 / Level 1) for a central or three-head heat pump, for invoices from July 6, 2026.

cards.title: Insulation
cards.note: Attic, wall and basement or crawlspace work, paid per R-value added per square foot. Homes heated mainly by electricity only.

cards.title: Windows and doors
cards.note: $100 per opening, with a U-factor of 1.22 or lower.

cards.title: Heat pump water heater
cards.note: Only when it replaces an electric water heater.

cards.title: Solar panels
cards.note: $1,000 per kW, capped at half the cost, from an HPCN member installer.

cards.title: Battery storage
cards.note: Up to $1,500 on its own with solar, or up to $5,000 with Peak Saver enrolment.

cards.title: EV charger
cards.note: 50% of a new wall-mounted Level 2 charger, plus $200 for a power-management device.

sections: What the 2021 Census says about Richmond homes

About 26% of Richmond households live in homes built before 1981, the third-lowest share among the cities we cover, after Surrey and the Township of Langley. Even so, 7,175 are owner-occupied detached houses from that era. Overall, 71% of households own, and 30% live in detached houses. Major repairs were reported by 4.9% of households. Richmond's housing is newer on average, so air sealing and attic work are less urgent than in Victoria or Prince George, while heat pumps and water heaters often come first.
Who in Richmond is actually covered

BC Hydro's Home Renovation Rebates are for houses heated mainly by electricity. A Richmond house on baseboards can claim up to $4,000 for a whole-home heat pump and up to $1,000 for a heat pump water heater. A strata townhouse or condo is excluded from those programs and has its own BC Hydro condo program. If the house burns gas, only the income-qualified CleanBC route applies, at $3,500, $7,000 or $13,000 by level.

Richmond gets about 3.47 peak sun hours a day in our solar data, a little better than the Fraser Valley cities. BC Hydro pays $1,000 per kW up to $5,000 for solar and up to $5,000 for a battery when it is enrolled in Peak Saver. Those rebates need an HPCN member to design and install the system, and they are paid first come, first served while funding lasts, so check availability before you sign.

If your Richmond house is on electric heat, the heat pump rebate is the biggest return on a single decision. BC Hydro's rebate takes up to $4,000 off the bill. If you are on gas, consider insulation and windows first, since there is no BC Hydro heat pump rebate for you.

claim_steps: Find out whether your bills show electric, gas, oil or propane.
Ask for heat pump quotes from HPCN installers and for the load calculation.
Price the water heater at the same visit if the tank is electric.
If you own a townhouse in a strata, read the strata guide before booking.
Apply within six months of the invoice.
faq: Yes, electricity is BC Hydro. Gas, where lines exist, is FortisBC.
Do I need to replace baseboards to qualify?
The heat pump rebate requires the system to replace electric heat such as baseboards or an electric furnace.
Is solar worth it in Richmond?
The rebate is up to $5,000 and the area gets about 3.47 peak sun hours a day. The payback depends on your usage.
Why is Richmond's pre-1981 share low?
The 2021 Census puts it at 26%, because much of the city was built later.
